title: Cascade Systems onboarding orientation & runbook review
summary: Kickoff orientation for Cascade Systems onboarding. Covered project goals, success criteria, timeline, networking/ security constraints (VPC, SSO, retention), runbook structure, and pilot plan (1-week perf/latency benchmark then 4-week integration). Agreed next steps: send network diagram, security whitepaper, draft runbook, schedule benchmark window. Action items assigned for both sides.
topics: Network & security constraints (VPC peering, SAML, KMS)
Pilot scope: perf benchmarks and telemetry
action_items: Samir Gupta - Share Redwood onboarding runbook template and security whitepaper - 2026-01-23
Jonah Reed - Provide VPC CIDR ranges and firewall egress policy - 2026-01-22
Diego Alvarez - Schedule 1-hour benchmarking window + test prompts spreadsheet - 2026-01-26
Leah Morrison - Confirm SOC2/ISO requirements and list of in-scope data types - 2026-01-24
Priya Shenoy - Draft 4-week pilot plan and share milestones - 2026-01-25
next_steps: Redwood to email runbook template + security pack (AM)
Cascade to share network diagram & SAML IdP metadata
Schedule benchmark window next Tue or Wed (Diego + Jonah)
Set up sandbox API key and sample dataset for smoke tests
transcript:
00:00 Samir (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining — we really appreciate you carving out the time. Quick roll call?
00:06 Maya (Cascade): Hey Samir, Maya here — Head of MLOps.
00:09 Jonah (Cascade): Jonah, Platform.
:11 Leah (Cascade): Leah from security.
00:14 Priya (CSM): Priya here, customer success.
00:16 Diego (SE): Diego, solutions — I'll own the benchmark work.
00:20 Samir: Great. Goal for today is to align on scope, success criteria, and initial runbook items so we can kick the pilot next week. Should be pretty practical.
00:33 Maya: Yeah we want to validate latency/cost tradeoffs and confirm the networking model — we are restricted by our VPC egress rules, and our compliance team wants KMS integration.
00:47 Leah: Right, SOC2 controls are required, we also need immutable audit logs for any PII access, and SAML SSO for the console.
01:00 Samir: Totally. On the compliance side we have a security whitepaper and a SOC2 overview — we'll include KMS/HSM integration notes. Priya will share those.
01:12 Leah: When you say KMS/HSM notes, do you support customer-managed keys for hosted clusters or only on private deployments?
01:21 Diego: Quick clarification — hosted API supports envelope encryption with customer KMS for certain tiers, private deployments can use HSMs or bring-your-own keys. There's sometimes nuance in the dedicated offering.
01:35 Jonah: For network we need to know whether we should plan for VPC peering or a private link. Also do you require static IPs for egress? Our environment blocks wide egress.
01:46 Samir: Good question. We support either VPC peering or PrivateLink-style setup for private. For hosted, we can set up an egress IP allowlist; dedicated customers often prefer private connectivity. We'll get specifics for static IP ranges in the network doc.
02:02 Maya: Timeline wise we want a short pilot — 1 week of perf testing then a 4-week integration before wider rollout. Does that fit your standard flow?
02:12 Priya: That's a common cadence. We'll map milestones: smoke tests, perf benchmark, integration, then go/no-go.
02:18 Diego: For the perf bench, I'll need sample prompts and expected latency p95 targets. Do you have sequences lengths and concurrency estimates?
02:29 Jonah: Mostly chat use-cases, avg seq 300 tokens, few longer threads up to 1k tokens. Expected concurrency initial 5-10 qps, ramp to 50 qps in production.
02:41 Diego: Perfect. We'll recommend batching and caching hints in the runbook. Also note model choice matters — quantized smaller models change cost/latency tradeoffs.
02:52 Maya: We are evaluating both hosted and dedicated. Cost is important but also predictability. If we go dedicated, how long to provision GPUs?
03:02 Samir: Dedicated provisioning typically 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and contractual terms. There's also reserved capacity options. For fast time-to-value we recommend hosted pilot then decide.
03:15 Leah: From security POV, hosted is ok if audit logs and SSO/KMS are in place. But data residency and retention policies matter — we store regulated customer PII.
03:27 Priya: Noted. We'll include retention controls and data handling in the runbook. We also have options for on-prem packages if required.
03:36 Ethan (SRE): A practical question: do you have an SDK or is it all REST? We prefer languages — Go and Python.
03:43 Diego: We have SDKs for Python, Go, and Node. SDKs include streaming and structured outputs; we'll share quickstart samples.
03:51 Michelle (Product): Who is the primary SLAs contact? We need a escalation ladder in case of incidents during pilot.
03:57 Priya: We'll include an escalation path with contact points; Redwood provides an on-call for dedicated pilots and a success engineer during the initial integration.
04:08 Samir: Ok let's walk through the runbook outline — Priya, you might run this: onboarding checklist, infra prep (network, keys, roles), perf plan, observability, cost controls, rollback steps.
04:23 Priya: Yes. First section: prerequisites — IAM roles, VPC connectivity, allowed egress, SAML metadata, and a test dataset. Second: steps to obtain sandbox credentials and smoke test. Third: perf bench details and expected artifacts. Fourth: runbook for anomalies.
04:40 Maya: On dataset: we will provide an anonymized sample of chat logs and a few latency-sensitive prompts. Do you support prefix caching and KV cache hints?
04:51 Diego: We do; runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to speed repeated context. We'll instrument metrics to show cache hit rates.
05:02 Jonah: For observability, we need token-level cost estimates and latency histograms. Do you provide dashboards or do we plug into our Grafana?
05:12 Diego: Both — Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards. We can also ship metrics to your Grafana via export or prometheus endpoint for long-term retention.
05:24 Leah: Audit logs — can we pull logs into our SIEM? We need retention for 1 year for certain records.
05:33 Samir: Yes, logs can be exported to your SIEM or S3; retention is configurable depending on plan. We'll confirm specifics in the security pack.
05:45 Maya: Ok great. Can we talk about the pilot success criteria? We'll be looking for p95 latency under 350ms for chat generation at 5 qps, cost per 1k tokens under a target, and no PII leakage in outputs.
05:58 Diego: We'll set up automated evals to check quality regressions and use your prompts as regression suite. For latency, we'll run a synthetic workload and collect p50/p95/p99.
06:11 Samir: Also add operational metrics: error rate <0.5%, and availability 99.9% during pilot window.
06:21 Maya: Fine. For the integration week, we'll need a point of contact to triage issues quickly.
06:27 Priya: That will be Rina and Diego for technical, Samir for contractual. We'll be available during bench window.
06:34 Jonah: About costs — will you provide an estimate for the pilot and a projection for production given our concurrency ramp plan?
06:41 Samir: Yes, we'll share a cost projection spreadsheet. Diego will include recommendations on quantization and batching that affect costs.
06:50 Leah: Regarding private deployments — if later we need private control plane in VPC, how invasive is that to our network? Any agents or connectors running in our subnet?
06:59 Diego: Private deployments require a small set of control-plane connectors and optionally data plane components that run inside your VPC; they're designed to be minimal and can be configured for restricted egress. We'll include an architecture diagram.
07:13 Michelle: Any known limitations with multi-tenant models and regulatory data? We need to avoid cross-tenant data bleed.
07:20 Samir: For hosted we have tenant isolation at request and model level; dedicated or private ensures full isolation. We'll document data boundaries.
07:27 Maya: Great. Can we see an example runbook item?
07:30 Priya: Sure — step 1: obtain sandbox API key; step 2: configure allowlist egress; step 3: run smoke test script (we'll provide). If failure at step 3, escalate to Diego.
07:43 Jonah: Practical ask — can we get a temporary sandbox with throttling limits that mimic production?
07:49 Diego: Yes, sandbox can be configured with mock qps and quota. We'll spin one up after network details are confirmed.
07:56 Maya: What about rate limiting and backpressure? We need graceful degradation so UIs don't break.
08:02 Diego: Runtime supports streaming and chunked responses; we can set circuit breakers and fallback model variants for graceful degradation.
08:12 Leah: Audit again — we need to know which team members have console access, RBAC, and can we integrate with our SSO groups?
08:20 Priya: We support SAML/SCIM, and RBAC roles map to groups — we can draft a recommended mapping for your teams.
08:29 Ethan: Any constraints around tokenization differences across models? We use consistent costing for tokens.
08:35 Diego: Tokenization varies by model family; cost per token will mirror model tokenization. We'll include sample tokenization stats per model choice.
08:44 Maya: Ok, timeline recap — share runbook template and security docs by Friday, provide network CIDRs by Thursday, schedule bench next Tue/Wed.
08:55 Samir: Correct. Also we'll arrange a 60-minute deep-dive focused only on networking if needed.
09:03 Jonah: That might be needed — our firewall team is strict.
09:06 Priya: We'll loop them in once Jonah shares the diagram.
09:10 Maya: Quick question — are there automated regressions tied to prompt changes? We want to avoid quality drift after model swaps.
09:18 Diego: Redwood Optimize offers regression alerts and prompt set evals; we can attach your regression suite and alert on quality drops after rollouts.
09:27 Michelle: If we choose a dedicated cluster, can we run A/B rollouts between model versions?
09:32 Diego: Yes, we support canary/A-B style rollouts with traffic splits and automatic fallback policies.
09:39 Samir: Let's talk risk: single point of failure scenarios and fallbacks. Diego, can you summarize typical fallback policies?
09:45 Diego: Sure — traffic split to a smaller but faster model, regional failover, and graceful per-request retries with jitter. Also pre-warmed caches for high-traffic routes.
09:58 Leah: Are logs encrypted at rest and in transit? Also key rotation policies?
10:03 Samir: Yes, logs are encrypted in transit and at rest; KMS-based key rotation supported. We'll include our key rotation SLA in the security pack.
10:14 Maya: Ok I'm going to hand off operational details to Jonah and Leah — they'll coordinate on network and security.
10:20 Jonah: I'll share a diagram and the CIDR ranges by Thursday EOD.
10:25 Leah: I'll send the list of compliance artefacts we need and confirm PII scope.
10:30 Priya: On Redwood side Priya will draft runbook and Samir will share contractual notes.
10:35 Samir: Diego will set up benchmark plan and mock sandbox once we have network details.
10:40 Maya: Any blockers we haven't surfaced?
10:43 Michelle: Only one — we need to ensure the product team can rerun automated evals with our prompt set.
10:49 Diego: Yes, we'll provide access to the eval harness and a short notebook to run locally.
10:54 Samir: Great — recap and next steps: Redwood sends runbook & security pack; Cascade sends network diagram, SAML metadata; schedule bench. Meeting for deep-net if needed.
11:10 Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
11:14 Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and action items.
11:20 (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings: e.g., "VPC peering" transcribed as "VPC pairing" in a few places; proper nouns may be slightly off. There was light crosstalk during rollcall.
